definitions.explanation: The physical ability to perceive through the senses (sight, hearing, touch, etc.).
An intuitive understanding or awareness; a knack for something.

examples.japanese: {痛|いた}みの{感覚|かんかく}がない。
examples.english: I have no sensation of pain.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{音楽|おんがく}の{感覚|かんかく}がいい。
examples.english: He has a good sense for music.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}の{感覚|かんかく}を{失|うしな}う。
examples.english: To lose one's sense of time.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}くて{手|て}の{感覚|かんかく}がなくなった。
examples.english: It was so cold that I lost sensation in my hands.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{間|あいだ}{海外|かいがい}に{住|す}んでいると、{日本語|にほんご}の{感覚|かんかく}が{鈍|にぶ}くなることがある。
examples.english: When you live abroad for a long time, your sense of the Japanese language can become dull.

examples.japanese: {麻酔|ますい}をかけたので、{下半身|かはんしん}の{感覚|かんかく}がまったくない。
examples.english: Since I was given anesthesia, I have no sensation at all in my lower body.

notes:
{感覚|かんかく} refers to both physical senses and intuitive understanding.

THE FIVE SENSES:
- {視覚|しかく} (vision)
- {聴覚|ちょうかく} (hearing)
- {触覚|しょっかく} (touch)
- {味覚|みかく} (taste)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく} (smell)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {感覚|かんかく}がいい/するどい (have good sense, be perceptive)
- {感覚|かんかく}が{鈍|にぶ}い (have dull senses)
- 〜の{感覚|かんかく} (sense of ~)

COMPOUND WORDS:
- {感覚|かんかく}{器官|きかん} (sensory organ)
- {感覚|かんかく}{的|てき} (sensory, intuitive)

HOMOPHONE:
- {間隔|かんかく} (interval, space) - different meaning
